## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Anekavaṇṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 82, also designated Vv 7.8) belongs to the *Vimānavatthu* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [Radich 2007]. In this text, a celestial youth (*deva*) explains to Mahā-Moggallāna that he attained his splendid celestial rebirth through the merit of encouraging others to revere the relics (*dhātu*) of the past Buddha Sumedha following that Buddha's *parinirvāṇa* [Radich 2007].

In modern scholarship on Buddhist somatic and devotional traditions, the text is cited alongside other *Vimānavatthu* narratives as canonical evidence for early relic veneration, illustrating how exhorting companions to pay homage to the relics of an enlightened being was held to secure a heavenly rebirth [Radich 2007].

**Sources**

- [Radich 2007] Michael David Radich, The Somatics of Liberation: Ideas about Embodiment in Buddhism from Its Origins to the Fifth Century C.E. (2007) — Discussed the interlocutors, the Buddha Sumedha relic narrative, and the role of the text in early Buddhist relic veneration.
